U1.quote: Another note is that the Gaia transformations are caused by the Nu-Baol seeding, which I believe we got from an Astral rift event. We periodically acquire pops (including through Nu-Baol seeding) but they're quickly assimilated into the main Lumieran species. canon_adopted: Newcomers who mechanically join the main Lumièran species keep their physical appearance, culture and individual identity, and remain free to change their appearance.

adopted: Player confirmation that the Gaia transformations were caused by Nu-Baol seeding — corroborated by the saves for four worlds; not for Éden (2242), which predates the Last Baol relic.
Player account that acquired pops are quickly assimilated into the main Lumièran species — consistent with the species reports, which list each newcomer species in one save only.
not_adopted: “which I believe we got from an Astral rift event” — explicitly tentative, and contradicted by the installed scripts and saves: life-seeding comes from activating the Last Baol relic, a Baol dig-trail reward. The Siege on Paradise rift yielded the Astral Cloaking edict.

entries.title: Terre
entries.lede: Capital of the République and the world where a dwindling humanity refused to end.

body.t: Before the playable campaign, the Gommage — an endemic catastrophe taking ever younger people — pushed humanity toward extinction. The Dessendres' work in artificial intelligence and robotics sustained society as the population fell and helped France become the dominant surviving power; that is why the République speaks French. Mind storage came first, but stored minds could not be restored; repeated biological cures failed.

The save timeline records the République's origin as Synthetic Fertility at the campaign start (2200.01.01), the first robot on Terre on 2203.04.01, and the synthesization milestone on 2216.04.21. The campaign's canon treats that last date as the moment synthetic embodiment became the decisive survival path.

Uploads work by every test available in the setting. The Lumièrans are living people whose memories and relationships continue — not imitations of the dead. Whether a soul survives is a claim opponents make, not a demonstrated failure.
Terre is saved as a Continental World through the 2370.01.01 snapshot and as a Gaia World from 2370.07.01.

Inside that interval, on 2370.01.14, the République's Baol life-seeding flag was re-set: a Nu-Baol life-seeding completed. The flag does not name a planet; Terre is identified by inference, as the only world in the archive that became Gaia in that six-month interval. The decision takes 720 days to enact, and when it was begun is not saved.

The user confirms that the Gaia transformations were caused by Nu-Baol seeding. Here the saves agree on the cause and date the completion; the species reports, unusually, list no Nu-Baol newcomers at Terre in the next save.
Terre is the capital in every retained save from 2214.01.01 to 2454.05.05, and Sol never leaves République control in the archive.

entries.title: Mars
entries.lede: Sol's second home: barren for most of the archive, then terraformed and settled.

body.t: Mars is saved as a Barren World through 2296.07.01 and as a Continental World from 2297.01.01, so the terraforming completed between those two saves.

A colony reference with République ownership first appears in the 2302.07.01 save, but the game timeline records the new colony on 2303.09.01. The earlier observation is best read as the colony being founded or under way; the exact colonization record is the 2303 date.

Planet flags in the latest save include terraforming and colony-event markers (barren_terraform, terraformed_once, colony_event), consistent with a terraformed then colonized world. They describe the world as of 2454.05.05, not when each flag was set.

entries.title: Saturn Interstellar Assembly
entries.lede: A monument to recognition. Influence and relationships did what the République's fleets could not.

body.t: The Ruphaari Protectors repeatedly humiliated the République over synthetic existence. Maëlle accepted their demands when resisting risked a hopeless war; Gustave told her plainly, “We can't face them.” In the campaign story, the Assembly around Saturn was the diplomatic answer: influence and recognition ended a pattern that immediate military resistance could not.
The save backs the Saturn placement: megastructure 221 is anchored to Saturn (planet 15) in Sol.

The République's built_interstellar_assembly_site flag carries the timestamp 2324.09.12, matching the game timeline's megastructure record. The construction site (stage 0) is first observed in the 2325.01.01 save.

Successive stages appear in the 2329.01.01, 2332.07.01 and 2335.07.01 saves, and the completed Assembly (stage 4) first appears in 2338.01.01. Sol's interstellar_assembly_built flag, which the game sets when the final stage completes, carries 2337.11.05.

Correction: the campaign personality records 2324.09.12 as the Assembly's completion. The saves show that date marks the start of construction (the site milestone); completion is 2337.11.05. The personality file was left unchanged for the user to decide.

entries.title: Azure Chalice
entries.fr: Le Grand Dormeur, intégré en paix
entries.lede: Capital of the Empire of Great Sleeper, a stronger neighbor that became fellow citizens.

body.t: In the earliest retained save (2214.01.01), the Empire of Great Sleeper is a hegemonic-imperialist despotic state whose capital is Azure Chalice in the Great Sleeper system. Its founding species is Sorann; campaign lore keeps them distinct from the Gestrals.

On 2225.01.19 the save timeline records the République's first subject. The 2270.01.01 save shows that relationship as a protectorate agreement added on 2225.01.19, last changed on 2262.05.07, with integration permitted. At that point the Empire still holds 62 systems.

By 2270.07.01 the Great Sleeper system and the Empire's former territory are République-owned; the old country record remains only as a residue holding no systems. Integration completed between the 2270.01.01 and 2270.07.01 saves.

Campaign canon establishes the integration as peaceful. The former inhabitants joined the République's democracy as citizens with their own cultures, ethics and factions. How their consent was expressed was never specified, so no plebiscite is assumed here.

Like every people who joins, the Great Sleeper's former citizens may merge mechanically into the main Lumièran species and still keep their own appearance, culture and individual identity (see Many Peoples, Shared Continuity).
Azure Chalice is saved as an Arctic World through 2359.07.01 and as a Gaia World from 2360.01.01.

Inside that interval, on 2359.12.12, a Nu-Baol life-seeding completed (the République's life-seeding flag was re-set). The flag names no planet; Azure Chalice is identified by inference, as the only world that became Gaia in that interval, consistent with the user's account. The 2360.01.01 species report carries a brief administrative trace of Nu-Baol at Azure Chalice (reported population 0.00, not a measured population); the 2360.07.01 save no longer shows it.

The BioGenesis event bio.3210 (“Biosphere Modified”) can mark a world with fe_world_of_thought, a biosphere modification. It is not a planet-class change, and the atlas does not treat it as the cause of the Gaia change.
Azure Chalice carries the fe_world_of_thought flag in the 2390.07.01 save. When it was applied is not retained.

entries.title: Wenkwort and the Eternal Hall
entries.lede: A natural-spectacle system that entered the République with the Great Sleeper.

body.t: Wenkwort is generated by the installed Federations initializer wenkwort_initializer, which flags it as a natural-spectacle system (wenkwort_system, natural_spectacle_system).
The system belonged to the Empire of Great Sleeper from its first observed owner (2217.01.01) through 2270.01.01, and to the République from 2270.07.01, in step with the integration.
The Eternal Hall carries the disrupted_garden flag. The installed on-action event action.495 sets it on the Wenkwort Artem world. The saves keep the flag but not the event's narrative circumstances.

A vluur_system star flag was set here on 2375.08.24 (its timestamp lies inside the bracketing snapshot interval); earlier saves place the same flag on Cormaggas and Vorsham. The archive does not retain what the Vluur did here.

Pérennité, Wenkwort's other world, was terraformed from Barren to Continental between the 2309.01.01 and 2309.07.01 saves. It became a Gaia World between 2380.01.01 and 2380.07.01. The fourth Nu-Baol life-seeding completed inside that interval, on 2380.06.02; the flag names no planet, and Pérennité is identified by inference as the only world to become Gaia then. The 2380.07.01 species report carries a brief administrative trace of Nu-Baol at Pérennité (reported population 0.00); the next save, 2380.07.24, no longer shows it.

entries.title: Éden and the Grunur Ruins
entries.lede: Alpha Centauri, one jump from Sol, where the République's first dig began the Baol trail.

body.t: The timeline records the first precursor discovery on 2200.11.01. Alpha Centauri's first_grunur_site0 flag and the République's baol_intro flag both decode to 2200.10.09. That is before the oldest retained save, so the date rests on the flag encoding (validated against the saved timeline) rather than on a snapshot interval.

The Grunur Ruins dig was completed in two chapters, on 2212.03.13 and 2213.09.13 — both before the oldest retained save, so these are the only surviving dates. The retained chapter events are “The Baol Organism” (twice), the second pointing toward a former Baol colony.
Éden was the République's second colony; the timeline records it on 2223.03.01. It is saved as a Continental World through 2242.01.01 and as a Gaia World from 2242.07.01.

That Gaia change was not the Baol's work. Éden carries the abandoned_terraforming_planet flag from the “Abandoned Terraforming Equipment” colony event. The République's “Resume Process” special project is listed from the 2226.07.01 save, and between the 2242.01.01 and 2242.07.01 saves Éden's saved modifier changes from abandoned_terraforming to gaia_world — the Gaia outcome of that chain.
This change came about ninety years before the République first held the Last Baol relic (first held in the 2333.01.01 save), so it cannot have come from that relic.

In the installed chain, an unknown agency's interrupted terraforming can be dismantled for research or resumed; a resumed process ends in one of several outcomes, one of which (colony.106) stabilizes the world as a Gaia World.
Alpha Centauri later hosted the République's Mega Art Installation, which reached its final stage by 2376.01.01.

entries.title: The Bleached Planet
entries.fr: La faille la plus proche de Sol
entries.lede: The astral rift closest to Sol, one hyperlane jump away, first seen under République exploration in the 2289 save and finished by the 2295 save.

body.t: Of all 80 astral-rift records, rift 6 in Alpha Centauri is the nearest to Sol, both by map distance and by hops (one hyperlane jump). It is first observed in the 2265.01.01 save, waiting for an explorer.
A République explorer was assigned between the 2288.07.01 and 2289.01.01 saves, and the rift is finished from 2295.01.01.

The retained chapters follow an ashen world: “Ashen Environment”, “Bleached Landscape”, “Rock Creatures”, “Bio-Geology”, “Darkest Before the Dawn”, and finally “Black Light Blinded”. The République's recorded choices included “Prepare for contact” and “Examine a rock creature”, and it retreated to the Rift Sphere at the Bio-Geology stage. The last chapter's saved outcome left scientist Jeanne Guérin with both Spark of Genius II and the Black Light Blinded trait.

entries.title: The Baol Trail
entries.lede: Across a century, four digs followed a vanished living precursor to a hidden system.

body.t: After the Grunur Ruins (2212–2213), the République completed “The Barren” on Scottica VIIIa (chapters 2220.12.09 → 2224.04.09), “The Shattered” on V413-AT in Elnath (2253.11.13 → 2257.01.21), and “The Silenced” on Siyieuzuno I (2331.03.25 → 2331.09.25). Each earlier dig ended by issuing the next “Former Baol Colony Investigation” special project.
The République's last_baol_system flag is timestamped 2332.02.13. The Grunur system first exists in the 2332.07.01 save — it is generated by the chain, not present earlier.
The relic The Last Baol is first held in the 2333.01.01 save (absent at 2332.07.01).

Activating the relic unlocks the planet decision “Nu-Baol Life-Seeding”. Gene-tailored plants carrying the Baol's gift of organic terraforming turn the world into a Gaia World and bring a group of Nu-Baol into being. The completion event re-sets the empire's has_used_baol_lifseeding flag every time.

That flag carries four successive values in the saves: 2338.12.19, 2359.12.12, 2370.01.14 and 2380.06.02. Each falls inside the save interval in which exactly one world in the archive became Gaia — Mélèze, Azure Chalice, Terre and Pérennité, in that order. The flag never names a planet, so each world is identified by that inference, which matches the user's account; brief Nu-Baol species traces appear at three of those worlds in the following save.
Clarification: Éden's earlier Gaia change (2242) came from abandoned alien terraforming, not from the Baol or this relic.
Clarification: the life-seeding comes from this relic, not from the Siege on Paradise rift, whose reward was the Astral Cloaking edict.
The relic kept working after 2390: the flag was re-set on 2390.07.19, 2401.06.01, 2411.06.07, 2441.07.26 and 2451.07.29, nine seedings in all.

entries.title: Siege on Paradise
entries.lede: Inside a rift at Poaa, the République found the Baol under threat and chose to hide them.

body.t: Rift 45 at Poaa is first observed in 2361.01.01. A République explorer is first observed in the 2362.07.01 save (assigned after 2362.01.01), and the rift is first observed finished in the 2372.01.01 save.

Retained choices, in order: “Contact the planet's inhabitants”, “Disclose what we know about the Baol”, “We will help however we can”, then at “Saving the Baol” the second option, “Deploy experimental planetary cloaking” (costing 50 astral threads), and finally “A suitable compromise”. The saved outcome made the Astral Cloaking edict available, and the République's astral_cloaking_available flag is timestamped 2371.10.25.
These choices come from this campaign's own saves. Option text is mapped from the installed astral_rift event definitions.

This rift's reward was the Astral Cloaking edict, not Nu-Baol life-seeding. The user recalled the seeding as an astral-rift reward, but the scripts and saves trace it to the Last Baol relic from the Baol dig trail; the first seeding (2338) predates this rift (first observed 2361).

entries.title: Mélèze
entries.lede: The first world the République turned into a garden with the Baol's gift.

body.t: Mélèze, in Electra, is saved as an Alpine World through 2338.07.01 and as a Gaia World from 2339.01.01.

Inside that interval the République's life-seeding flag was set for the first time, on 2338.12.19 — the first Nu-Baol life-seeding, six years after the last Baol system was found. The flag names no planet; Mélèze is identified by inference, as the only world in the archive that became Gaia in that interval.

The 2339.01.01 species report carries a brief administrative trace of Nu-Baol at Mélèze (reported population 0.00, not a measured population); the 2339.07.01 save no longer shows it. Under campaign canon, newcomers who join the Lumièran species keep their own appearance and culture.

The Rubricator is first held in the 2325.07.01 save, the first save after the final chapter.
Zoldiore later hosted the République's Science Nexus (think tank), which reached its final stage by 2350.01.01.

entries.title: The Advisor at Nekkar
entries.lede: A helpful presence inside a rift, and a scientist who stayed behind with it.

body.t: Rift 11 is first observed under République exploration in the 2317.07.01 save and first observed finished in 2320.07.01. Choices: “Ask for assistance”, “Ask for FURTHER assistance”, and “Wait, come back!”. The saved outcome records scientist Armand Noël as exiled: he chose to stay with the advisor.
The installed script does not end there. Exiling him also schedules a follow-up 1,800 days later that returns the lost explorer aboard a science ship and marks him “rift-warped”.

The saves bear that out. Armand Noël is absent from the République's leaders from the 2320.07.01 save through 2325.01.01, and is back in the 2325.07.01 save with the new rift-warped trait. The 2325.01.05 recruitment date saved for him is a field value, not proof of the exact return date.
He is still serving in the 2454.05.05 save, now at level 8 and recognised as an expert in dig sites and astral rifts.

entries.title: Esquie
entries.lede: The République's tamed L-Drake, he/him. A mobile companion, not a fixed place.

body.t: The tamed L-Drake is Esquie, referred to as he/him. The user likes Maëlle riding him, echoing Expedition 33. His presence brings affection and wonder into a civilization otherwise preoccupied with survival. A reincarnation or ancient shared past with Maëlle was suggested but never established.
When the L-Cluster opened (global flag timestamp 2361.07.06), a young dragon spawned at Entropy's Maw, a République L-Gate system. The same date marks the dragon point at Talan.

Ship 33556718, an “Immature Specimen” of the nanite young-dragon design, is first observed at Talan in 2362.01.01, held by the Freed Dragons. Between the 2369.01.01 and 2369.07.01 saves it passed to the République; the République's visited_dragon_point flag is timestamped 2368.09.12. It is observed at Electra in 2370.07.01 and in Sol from 2371.01.01.

A special project to tame the L-Drake is open in the 2369.01.01 save and gone by 2369.07.01 — the same interval in which the hatchling passed to the République. The saves do not keep the taming's own date.
The fleet is first named “Esquie” in the 2390.07.01 save. Because he moves, his marker shows the latest observed system only.

entries.title: The Ruphaari Protectors
entries.lede: The spiritualist Fallen Empire that refused to recognize synthetic people.

body.t: The timeline records first contact with the Ruphaari Protectors on 2277.12.13. Their capital system is Grugmora.

The Ruphaari repeatedly humiliated the République over synthetic existence. Maëlle accepted their demands when resistance risked a hopeless war. Gustave's counsel was unequivocal: endure, protect Maëlle and the population, and keep looking for a way out. The République never agreed that its people are counterfeit.

In a separate ultimatum, a Fallen Empire demanded a junior scientist, imagined as a tearful volunteer willing to go so the République could continue. Which Fallen Empire made that demand is not established, so it is not placed here.

entries.title: Tortoka Commonality
entries.lede: A subject at the center of the République's investigation into Lumièran servitude.

body.t: The timeline records Tortoka as a new subject on 2375.07.22, under a protectorate agreement that, in the 2390.07.01 save, does not permit integration; by then Tortoka was also a member of the République's federation. The agreement is first listed as integration-permitted in the 2418.07.01 save. Between the 2420.01.01 and 2420.07.01 saves Tortoka leaves the reports, and both of its systems pass to the République.

Lumièrans appeared on the slave market, prompting rescue by purchase and an investigation. Tortoka was central to the concern; Glebsig and others also required scrutiny. The working reconstruction — emigrants from an earlier hard period, later descendants or new minds assembled into servitude — is a discussed reconstruction, not proof of any one person's history.

The proposed Loi sur la protection universelle de la personne consciente (Act on the Universal Protection of Conscious Persons) would require governments to end the servitude of conscious persons and permit military enforcement. No save records its passage; the wars that followed are traced in the journey on emancipation, without assigning them this cause.

entries.title: Union of Associated Nations
entries.lede: The République's federation: ten members in 2390 and again in 2454 — but by then every member except the République is its subject.

body.t: The République accepted an invitation to the Union of Associated Nations. The independent members discussed were the République, the Glebsig Foundation and the Korinth Augmented Grand Duchy; other members include subjects. A federation law places war declarations in the president's hands, so another presidency could draw the République into a war it would not choose.

At 2390.07.01 the République leads a level-5 federation whose members are Bilnoc, Vhellet, the Sacrosanct Bokasheran Theocracy, Pelx-Cradonian Consumer Products, Glebsig, Korinth, Dojack II, the Panuri Tranquil Alliance and Tortoka, with the Zracon Alliance as an associate.

The 2390.07.01 save itself names the federation: its saved name nests “Union of” and “Associated Nations”, which renders as the Union of Associated Nations — the same name the campaign uses. The analyzer reports omit the name, so it is read from a pinned save record.

Between the 2429.07.01 and 2430.01.01 saves, five members leave: Glebsig, Korinth, the Sacrosanct Bokasheran Theocracy, Pelx-Cradonian and the Panuri Tranquil Alliance. Bilnoc and Tortoka had already gone by integration (2416.01.01 and 2420.07.01 saves). The Giranshu Galactic Mandate, an associate since the 2398.01.01 save, becomes a member in the 2435.07.01 save, together with Blessed Torrent.

In the 2454.05.05 save the federation has ten members again: the République and nine République subjects — Dojack II, Vhellet, Giranshu, Blessed Torrent, Zracon, Breanne, Pelx-Cradonian, Panuri Tranquil and Korinth. The République is its president.

entries.title: The République in 2454
entries.lede: Where the archive now ends: the galaxy's leading power, at peace itself, presiding over a federation of its own subjects.

body.t: In the 2454.05.05 save — the newest of 485 snapshots — the République holds 307 systems and 73 colonies with 4072.92 pops, and ranks first in victory score. At the edition-3 cutoff (2390.07.01) it held 221 systems and 50 colonies with 2488.30 pops.

Maëlle (leader 922746908) is the saved ruler in every one of the 485 snapshots. Since 2390 the timeline records elections on 2393.10.11, 2404.04.11, 2414.10.11, 2425.04.11, 2435.10.11 and 2446.04.11; in each case the saved ruler in the snapshots on either side is Maëlle. The saves do not record who stood, how votes were cast, or the margin.

A democracy whose president has served for more than two and a half centuries is the République's paradox in miniature: continuity is its founding promise, and every election is also a question about whether continuity of one person is what its citizens choose. The atlas records the tenure; it does not judge the elections.

The République is not a belligerent in any war in the 2454.05.05 save. Two wars are active elsewhere, both against the Wandering Sek-Lokkar: one led by the Wandering Ti-Zru (started 2429.07.01), one by the Imperium of Torix with four allies (started 2438.09.24).

Its nine subjects in the latest save are Dojack II, the Vhellet Assembly, the Giranshu Galactic Mandate, the Blessed Torrent Sovereignty, the Zracon Alliance, the Breanne Empire, Pelx-Cradonian Consumer Products, the Panuri Tranquil Alliance and the Korinth Augmented Grand Duchy. All nine are members of the République's federation; no independent state is.

Between the two editions the République fought three wars of subjugation (declared 2429.07.01, 2442.10.08 and 2447.09.25), integrated three long-standing subjects, saw five federation partners leave and three return as subjects, and completed five more Nu-Baol life-seedings.

The galaxy's own timeline marks a Voidworm plague on 2397.01.01 and the rise of a Great Khan on 2421.03.18; the République first holds the Khan's Throne relic between the 2423.01.01 and 2423.07.01 saves. How it came by the throne is not recorded.

The founding promise and its unresolved edge are unchanged: no one should die again, and the République still has not settled whether a person may refuse continued existence, or how far its protection of conscious persons may be enforced on others.

entries.title: Three Wars of Subjugation
entries.lede: 2429–2452: the République's first wars of choice in a century, each ending with the defeated as protectorates or vassals.

body.t: On 2429.07.01 the République declared war. The timeline's declaration record names the Nomadic Adeex; the saved war goal, read from the raw war block, is the subjugation of the Blessed Torrent Sovereignty. Dojack II and the Vhellet Assembly fought alongside it against Blessed Torrent, the Nomadic Adeex, Uriy Dynamics and the Imperium of Torix. The war was won on 2435.02.30, and a protectorate agreement with Blessed Torrent is dated that day.

The Giranshu Galactic Mandate also became a République subject, under a bulwark agreement, on 2435.02.30. Giranshu is not listed among that war's participants, so the atlas does not count it as a war outcome.

On 2442.10.08 the République declared war again. The declaration record names the Council of Neetris, Glebsig's subject; the saved goal is the subjugation of the Breanne Empire. The defenders were Breanne, Glebsig, the Council of Neetris, the Zracon Alliance, the Sacrosanct Bokasheran Theocracy and the Holy Panuri Grand Duchy — most of the rival federation Breanne led. The République won on 2447.02.19, and protectorate agreements with Breanne and Zracon are dated that day. Glebsig and the Council of Neetris remained independent of the République.

On 2447.09.25 a third war followed. The declaration record names Pelx-Cradonian Consumer Products; the saved goal is the subjugation of the Korinth Augmented Grand Duchy, which was joined by Pelx-Cradonian and the Panuri Tranquil Alliance. Every earlier victim of the République — Blessed Torrent, Breanne and Zracon — fought on its side, along with Giranshu, Dojack II and the Vhellet Assembly. The war was won on 2452.01.01, and agreements with Korinth (protectorate), Pelx-Cradonian (bulwark) and the Panuri Tranquil Alliance (vassal, oppressive terms) are dated that day.

Korinth, Pelx-Cradonian and the Panuri Tranquil Alliance had left the République's federation between the 2429.07.01 and 2430.01.01 saves; they are listed as members again from the 2452.07.01 save, now as subjects.

Campaign canon describes a proposed war-powers instrument against servitude and the image of Maëlle leading a crusade (C6). The saves show wars of subjugation, not their reasons: no casus belli, law or speech is recorded. Some targets did permit servitude at the time — Breanne allowed slavery, and Korinth, Pelx-Cradonian and Zracon held AI in servitude — but others, such as Blessed Torrent, did not. Read these wars beside the canon, not as its proof.

entries.title: Three Integrations
entries.lede: Bilnoc, Tortoka and the Panuri Divine Theocracy: long-standing subjects whose agreements came to permit integration, and who then joined the République.

body.t: Bilnoc Star Conglomerate had been a République subject since 2290.07.26. Its agreement is first listed as permitting integration in the 2409.01.01 save. Between the 2415.07.01 and 2416.01.01 saves the agreement disappears, the country is no longer in the reports, and all 32 of its systems are République-owned.

Tortoka Commonality, a subject since 2375.07.22, is first listed as integration-permitted in the 2418.07.01 save. Between the 2420.01.01 and 2420.07.01 saves it leaves the reports, and both of its systems pass to the République.

The Panuri Divine Theocracy, a subject since 2315.11.13 after the Panuri war, is first listed as integration-permitted in the 2425.01.01 save. Between the 2431.01.01 and 2431.07.01 saves it leaves the reports, and all 25 of its systems are République-owned. Until its last listed save, the 2431.01.01 save, the Theocracy's policies allowed slavery and held AI in servitude.

Under the game's rules, an integrated subject's population joins the overlord and lives under the overlord's policies. In the République's case these are no slavery and full AI rights (policy_state.tsv). The saves show the change of state, not the experience of any individual.
The Blessed Torrent Sovereignty's protectorate is first listed as integration-permitted in the 2443.07.01 save. It is still a subject in the 2454.05.05 save.

Canon holds that integrated peoples keep their cultures, appearance and individual identity while joining the République's democracy, as the Great Sleeper's people did. How each subject's consent was expressed is not specified, and no plebiscite is assumed.

entries.title: The Union Divided
entries.lede: Between two saves in 2429 five partners left the Union of Associated Nations; a rival federation, led first by Breanne and then by Glebsig, took shape.

body.t: Glebsig, Korinth, the Sacrosanct Bokasheran Theocracy, Pelx-Cradonian Consumer Products and the Panuri Tranquil Alliance are all listed as members of the République's federation in the 2429.07.01 save and are absent from it in the 2430.01.01 save. The Zracon Alliance, an associate, leaves between the 2430.07.01 and 2431.01.01 saves.

The République declared its first war of the period on 2429.07.01, the date of the last save that still lists them. The saves do not record why the five left or in what order, so the atlas does not connect the two.

A new federation carries the saved start date 2430.12.25. It is first listed in the 2431.01.01 save, led by the Breanne Empire with Glebsig as its only other member. It grew over the next saves: Pelx-Cradonian and the Akkano Concord are listed by the 2432.07.01 save; the Council of Neetris, the Bokasheran Theocracy, the Holy Panuri Grand Duchy and Zracon by the 2434.01.01 save; and Korinth from the 2439.07.01 save.

The République's 2442 war, whose saved goal was Breanne, was fought against most of that federation: Breanne, Glebsig, the Council of Neetris, Zracon, the Bokasheran Theocracy and the Holy Panuri Grand Duchy. Breanne and Zracon became République protectorates on 2447.02.19, and from the 2447.07.01 save the rival federation is led by Glebsig. In the 2454.05.05 save it has two members, Glebsig and its subject the Council of Neetris.
Glebsig is still independent in the 2454.05.05 save. It holds the second-largest Lumièran population outside the République.

Canon names the République, Glebsig and Korinth as the federation's three independent members and notes a law placing war declarations in the president's hands — a power that could draw partners into wars they would not choose. Canon does not say whether that tension caused the split.

entries.title: Lumièrans Beyond the République
entries.lede: Lumièrans live in a dozen foreign states, and once appeared on the slave market. What the saves can and cannot say.

body.t: Campaign canon records that Lumièrans appeared on the slave market, that the République rescued people by purchase and release, and that it investigated how their population came to exist abroad. The working reconstruction is not proof of any individual's history.

The 2379.07.01 save — before the edition-3 cutoff, newly found for this edition — lists 15 pops of the Lumièran species, robotic, on the galactic slave market. It is the only Lumièran listing in any of the 485 saves; 41 saves list anything at all. The seller is not established, and the saves do not show who bought them.

The species reports count Lumièran pops in other countries in every save. In the 2454.05.05 save there are about 579 in the Korinth Augmented Grand Duchy, 417 in Glebsig, 116 in Blessed Torrent, 47 in Uriy Dynamics and 21 in Giranshu. Korinth's count roughly tripled from about 190 in the 2390.07.01 save.

Korinth's AI policy is AI Servitude in every save from 2364.07.01 to 2454.05.05. The installed definition says such machines are held “in absolute servitude” and barred from ruler jobs. Lumièrans are a robotic species, but the reports do not show the status the engine gives each of them.

Korinth has been a République protectorate since 2452.01.01. Its AI Servitude policy is unchanged in the 2454.05.05 save, as are Pelx-Cradonian's (AI Servitude and slavery allowed) and Zracon's (AI Servitude), and Breanne still allows slavery. Becoming a République subject did not, by itself, change any of these policies.

Canon warns that taking a state as a subject does not prove its internal servitude has ended. In 2454 that is the République's open question: its protection now extends over states whose laws still deny artificial minds the rights the République grants its own.

entries.title: The Later Gardens
entries.lede: Five more worlds turned Gaia by the Last Baol relic between 2390 and 2452 — and how the République's twelve Gaia worlds came to be.

body.t: The République's life-seeding flag was re-set five more times after the edition-3 cutoff: on 2390.07.19, 2401.06.01, 2411.06.07, 2441.07.26 and 2451.07.29. In each case exactly one world in the archive turned Gaia in the same six-month interval: Fontaine (Sirius), Nuitz's Treasure (Tarazed), The Wait (Ancastar), Églantine (Maaz) and Where Nuitz Spoke (Wum Jiam). The worlds are identified by that coincidence; the flag names no planet.
Églantine had been a Nuked world since the 2268.07.01 save, before the Great Sleeper's integration, and was seeded nearly two centuries later. Where Nuitz Spoke was the Great Sleeper's Arctic world.

In the 2454.05.05 save the République holds twelve Gaia worlds: nine life-seeded; Éden, turned Gaia in 2242 by the separate Abandoned Terraforming chain; and two that were Gaia in every save in which they appear — the Eternal Hall of Wenkwort, and Félicité (Joinum II), first observed as a République colony in the 2412.07.01 save and recorded as a new colony on 2413.05.01.

Only The Wait shows the brief Nu-Baol species trace that earlier seedings left, in the 2411.07.01 save. Nine other worlds turned Gaia over the same years, all uncolonized and in systems held by the Breanne Empire or Blessed Torrent at the time; none is attributed to the République's relic.

The user confirmed that Nu-Baol seeding causes the Gaia transformations, and that newcomers are quickly assimilated while keeping their appearance, culture and identity. A species row that vanishes is not a death.

entries.title: The Gommage
entries.lede: The catastrophe before the campaign: a plague of time that took ever younger people.

body.t: The Gommage is an endemic catastrophe taking progressively younger people. Population dwindles, institutions lose the people who sustain them, and the future shrinks into ever shorter reprieves. The République's refusal to accept death begins here. An earlier proposed explanation for the failed cure — that the apparent pathogen was also doing indispensable repair — remains a proposal.

entries.title: Verso and pVerso
entries.lede: The brother who could not be saved, and the artificial Verso who came after.

body.t: The original Verso died in a war during the age of catastrophe and could not be stored. An artificial Verso — pVerso — was created afterward, lived long in a virtual world, loved Maëlle, and later received a synthetic body. His existence is not the restoration of the original.
He wants an eventual death. That wish challenges Maëlle's mission at its most intimate point; his final choice and her response remain unwritten.

entries.title: Universal Protection of Conscious Persons
entries.fr: Loi sur la protection universelle de la personne consciente
entries.lede: A proposed war-powers instrument, embraced in concept but not established as enacted.

body.t: Conscious personhood does not depend on substrate or a foreign legal category. Conscious persons cannot be property, and manufacturing them creates no right to their service. The draft would let the Première Présidente enforce compliance when peaceful demands fail. Its enactment date and any crusade have not been established.

entries.title: Cosmogenesis
entries.lede: The adopted ambition to understand and overcome even cosmic limits, with its moral limits still unresolved.

body.t: Cosmogenesis grows from the conviction that even enormous limits can be understood and overcome through science; Gustave's engineering temperament and Maëlle's refusal to abandon the impossible make it intelligible. Which harms are acceptable on the way, and the final outcome, remain undecided.

At 2390.07.01, and still at 2454.05.05, the path stands at level III, with no owned Synaptic Lathe and no completed Horizon Needle (personality S6, cosmogenesis_status.tsv). In the latest save the next gate technology is offered but not yet researched.

entries.title: The Crystal Sphere
entries.lede: A chain begun in 2352 whose portal has not opened.

body.t: The global crystal_sphere_sent flag carries 2352.01.01. In 2390.07.01, and still in 2454.05.05, storyline_status.tsv lists the Azilash storyline as in progress, the portal not opened, no quest owner, and the République holding a rift sphere. No crystal rift near Sol and no completed Formless arc is implied.

entries.title: Many Peoples, Shared Continuity
entries.lede: Newcomers can join the Lumièran people without becoming the same: faces, cultures and lives stay their own.

body.t: The République periodically gains new people — including the Nu-Baol who arrive with each Baol life-seeding — and they are quickly assimilated into the main Lumièran species. Canonically, that mechanical merger is not the end of who they are: individuals keep their physical appearance and their culture, and they remain free to change their appearance if they choose.

The République is therefore not a population of identical-looking people. Species, citizenship, ancestry and culture are different things; a saved species label does not say who someone used to be or how they live.

The species reports show Nu-Baol at Mélèze, Azure Chalice and Pérennité, and Andari at The Gates of Loctl, only as brief administrative traces: each appears in a single save after the arrival, with reported population 0.00, and in no later retained save through 2390.07.01. These are not measured populations. This is consistent with the player-confirmed rapid assimilation; the reports do not track individual fates, and a row's absence is not evidence of death, migration or cultural erasure.

This is undated campaign canon, not a law enacted at a particular date. It applies equally to the Great Sleeper's former citizens, to newcomers from rifts and seedings, and to anyone else who joins. It does not settle the separate questions canon leaves open — whether a person may refuse continuation, or how far Maëlle's mission may go against someone's will.

Orbital telemetry shows a massive impact crater on the surface of Hazra IIIa. It was not caused by a meteorite strike, as the crater is surprisingly deep in proportion to its diameter. In fact, the actual depth cannot yet be determined, as the shaft is choked by rock debris part of the way down, blocking any further orbital scans.

It appears that a conventional excavation is the only way to find out what lies below.

entries.title: Kleptomaniac Rats
entries.lede: Archaeological site on Sérénité, Zoldiore.

body.t:
This planet has played host to a mammalian society of compulsive gatherers and hoarders. Their labyrinthine city is littered with junk, their towering ramshackle buildings pieced together from scraps of re-purposed materials. As far as the eye can see are mountains of knick-knacks, ornaments and artifacts.

The tiny ratlike inhabitants did not produce any goods of their own but were proficient spacefarers who likely pilfered the things they needed, as well as a whole lot of things they did not need, from other alien cultures.

entries.title: Too Angled
entries.lede: Archaeological site on Haftorang IIa, Haftorang.

body.t:
The surface of Haftorang IIa is utterly without precedent in all our exploration to date. Vast geological areas, from mountain ranges to entire continents, are suddenly cut by shapes far too geometrically regular to be natural in origin. The otherwise natural-looking environments are suddenly broken by entirely flat planes, perfect triangles and sharply-angled corners.

At present, any explanation of this baffling phenomenon is pure conjecture.

entries.title: Hidden Worlds
entries.lede: Archaeological site on Givre, Tem.

body.t:
A crashed alien space station has been unearthed on Givre after being buried for many millennia. The masterful construction previously held a self-contained arthropoid civilization of millions. Their dead bodies have been preserved within the station, making exploration of the otherwise magnificent interior an eerie endeavor.

Though the cause of their civilization's demise is not yet clear, the inhabitants perished suddenly, well before impact. Some died peacefully clutching tiny idols while others, bearing weapons, suffered violent trauma.

body.t: Status at 2454.05.05: finished. Last explorer: République de la Continuité. Saved rift owner: République de la Continuité.

Retained République choices, in order: “Deploy sample collection rig” (The Fluid); “Use emergency gases” (Snagged); “Explore the crystalline orifice” (The Chamber); “Pump exotic gases. Neutralize the beast” (The Blob); “Unfortunate” (Dissolved).

facts.t: The Fluid rift at Bartyam first observed
République de la Continuité explorer assigned to The Fluid rift
The Fluid rift: exploration in progress
The Fluid rift: exploration finished

chapters.context: The Sphere drifts in a pulsing red fluid through tubular passages — perhaps inside a giant organism. Deploy a sampling rig, or move freely?
chapters.branch: Chose “Deploy sample collection rig.” (other options: “Proceed forward at ease.”)
chapters.outcome_note: Saved tooltip recorded when the event fired; later consequences are evidenced only where other facts show them.

chapters.context: The sampling rig jams in a narrowing tunnel. Cut it loose, or burn exotic gases to tear free with the samples?
chapters.branch: Chose “Use emergency gases.” (other options: “Cut it loose. The risk isn't worth it.”)
chapters.outcome: −50 exotic gases, +40 astral threads. Research option gained: Cell Revitalization.
chapters.outcome_note: Saved tooltip recorded when the event fired; later consequences are evidenced only where other facts show them.
chapters.conditional_note: * conditional options: availability depends on the empire's traits or earlier choices.

chapters.context: Samples saved; the crew drifts for days and believes it is inside a super-organism. Follow the flow out, or enter a crystalline orifice?
chapters.branch: Chose “Explore the crystalline orifice.” (other options: “Follow the flow outward.”)
chapters.outcome_note: Saved tooltip recorded when the event fired; later consequences are evidenced only where other facts show them.

chapters.optText: Pump exotic gases. Neutralize the beast.
chapters.context: A starship-sized blob swallows the Sphere and begins digesting its hull. The tactical officer urges evacuation; the biologist thinks the right gases could neutralize its enzymes.
chapters.note: The République chose to pump in exotic gases (spending 100). In the installed script this gamble leads either to an escape chapter or, if a roll fails, to “Dissolved”; the retained next chapter is “Dissolved”, so the gamble failed.
chapters.branch: Chose “Pump exotic gases. Neutralize the beast.” (other options: “Pull anchor. Return immediately.”)
chapters.outcome_note: Saved tooltip recorded when the event fired; later consequences are evidenced only where other facts show them.
chapters.conditional_note: * conditional options: availability depends on the empire's traits or earlier choices.

chapters.context: Contact with the science team is lost. Standard procedure retracts the anchor and recovers what is left of the mostly dissolved Sphere, coated in a valuable biomass. The crew is commended for its bravery.
chapters.note: The saved outcome records that scientist Alain Fontaine died, with a ten-year biology research modifier from the samples. That the rift was a giant organism remained the crew's supposition.
chapters.branch: Acknowledged with the only option, “Unfortunate.”
chapters.outcome: +150 astral threads. Rift Fluid Samples modifier added for 10 Years: Research Speed (Biology): +10% Fraternité: Scientist Alain Fontaine dies The expedition ends.

entries.title: Maëlle Dessendre
entries.role: Première Présidente of the République de la Continuité; the save often calls her President Maëlle.

status.label: Office
status.value: Première Présidente (elected; not hereditary or lifetime by canon)

status.label: Saved traits (2454.05.05, unchanged since 2390.07.01)
status.value: Supreme Organizer, Principled, Politician, Synthetic, Embezzler, and others

entries.lede: The elected leader whose refusal of loss became a civilization's mission — sincere, democratic, and dangerous in its reach.

body.t: Maëlle leads a genuine democracy and repeatedly wins elections, with Gustave usually the runner-up. Her tenure reflects support, gratitude and ability, not fraud or a disguised monarchy. Her informal power still exceeds an ordinary officeholder's — canon's phrase is “a goddess pretending to be a peer”, an asymmetry of historical importance, not literal divinity.

Her founding ambition is that no one will die in the galaxy again. The original characterization explicitly includes bringing immortality to people whether they consent or not, supported by a democratic Lumièran electorate. Canon keeps this coercive edge visible and does not soften it into a purely voluntary program.
She prefers to avoid war but will use violence. A stronger opponent can force her to accept humiliation without her accepting their judgment, and a loved person can oppose her without her yielding.
The save's Embezzler trait has been given the headcanon of favoritism toward Verso and Gustave. It is an interpretation of a game trait, not an invented scandal.

Her attachment to the original Verso, and possibly her sense of responsibility for his death, is central to the backstory. The circumstances of his death and the basis of any guilt are deliberately unspecified.

Six elections are recorded in the timeline after 2390. In each, the saved ruler in the snapshots before and after is Maëlle, and she is the ruler in every save the archive holds. The saves record her tenure, not the votes.

entries.title: Gustave
entries.role: Engineer and problem-solver; Maëlle's principal electoral runner-up. Canon gives him no formal office.
entries.lede: The engineer who looks for a way through impossible constraints, and the voice that said “We can't face them.”

body.t: Gustave is an engineer before he is a spokesman for caution. His repeated second places make him a real political alternative inside a shared civic project, with no established feud or disloyalty.

Against a Fallen Empire the République cannot defeat, his counsel is unequivocal: “We can't face them.” Endure the humiliation, preserve Maëlle and the population, and keep working toward a solution — strategic patience, not permanent submission.

His Expedition 33 invention inspires the user's sense that he fits the République's Cosmogenesis ambition. No such device exists in this Stellaris timeline unless it is later established, and Expedition 33 episodes of his life are not imported into this alternate universe.

entries.title: Verso and pVerso
entries.role: The original Verso (dead, never preserved) and the artificial Verso (pVerso), a living person in his own right.

status.label: Original Verso
status.value: Died in war; not preserved; circumstances unspecified

status.label: pVerso
status.value: Living, synthetic body; wishes for eventual death

entries.lede: Two people who share a name: a brother who could not be saved, and the one who came after and wants, eventually, to die.

body.t: The original Verso died in a war during the age of catastrophe and could not be stored, so no preserved mind exists to recover. He built the first Gestrals.

An artificial Verso — pVerso — was created afterward, lived a long time in a virtual environment, developed a relationship with Maëlle, and later received a synthetic body. His existence is not the restoration of the original, and his affection and suffering are real.

He wants an eventual death. That wish challenges Maëlle's mission at its most intimate point. It is neither a bug to correct nor a right the République is established to guarantee. His final choice and her response remain unwritten.
In the established visual framing he stands slightly apart and subtly conflicted: attached, involved, capable of avoidance as well as devotion.

entries.title: Monoco and the Gestrals
entries.role: Monoco, an AI person whose personality is based on the family dog; the Gestrals, first built by the original Verso.

status.label: Continuity
status.value: Gestral mortality discussed; distinct from Lumièran immortality

entries.lede: Warmth and loyalty in a civilization of survivors — and a reminder that not every artificial being shares Lumièran immortality.

body.t: The original Verso created the first Gestrals, part of the Dessendres' history of robotics and companionship. Monoco is an AI whose personality is based on the family dog; a sapient Monoco is a person, not property.

The Gestrals have been discussed as not sharing the Lumièrans' immortality. Native Gestrals are not every population the save labels “Robot”, and the Great Sleeper's founding species is Sorann, not Gestral.

entries.title: Sciel and Lune
entries.role: Members of the intended companion ensemble; no offices or AU biographies are established.
entries.lede: Part of the ensemble around Maëlle — and deliberately left unwritten.

body.t: Sciel and Lune belong to the requested companion ensemble and appear in the visual conception beside Gustave, Verso and Monoco. Their formal offices and alternate-universe biographies have not been established; the atlas invents no ministries, marriages, deaths or commands for them.

entries.title: Esquie
entries.role: The République's tamed L-Drake (he/him). His evidenced history is in the Esquie story.

status.label: Map
status.value: Mobile; see the Esquie story for observed positions

entries.lede: Affection and wonder — and a saved trail from the opening of the L-Cluster to Sol.

body.t: The tamed L-Drake is Esquie, he/him. The user likes Maëlle riding him, echoing Expedition 33. A reincarnation of the original Esquie or an ancient shared past with Maëlle was suggested but never established.

entries.title: The Democratic République
entries.role: An interstellar democracy of individual persons with an elected presidency; official languages French and English.
entries.lede: A real democracy that can sincerely endorse a coercive universal mission.

body.t: The République is a society of individual persons with a democratic government — not a gestalt, not a disguised monarchy. Its political character is democratic, egalitarian and strongly materialist; French and English are official languages.

The 2454.05.05 save, like the 2390.07.01 save, shows democratic authority, a physical synthetic democracy government, the civics Beacon of Liberty, Masterful Crafters and Meritocracy, the Synthetic Fertility origin, and the capital Terre.

Former inhabitants of the Empire of Great Sleeper joined the same democracy after peaceful integration, keeping their cultures, ethics and factions. Nothing establishes a lesser franchise for them, and integration did not erase them as a people.

Conscious beings matter regardless of biological or synthetic origin; a maker does not own what it makes. Lumièran identity, citizenship, species ancestry and the save's “Robot” category are distinct things.

The democracy's support for Maëlle does not prove that everyone beyond its borders, or every dissenter within them, consents to what she intends. Popular legitimacy and the limits of what it settles both stay visible.

entries.title: Proposed Constitution
entries.role: French-inspired institutions proposed in discussion; only the elected presidency and democracy are established.
entries.lede: A coherent model to develop, not an adopted constitution.

body.t: Established: a genuine democracy with an elected presidency. The exact electoral method is unspecified.

Proposed: a directly elected Première Présidente as chief executive, foreign-policy leader and commander-in-chief; a unicameral Assemblée de la Continuité elected proportionally, which passes laws and authorizes offensive war; a Conseil des Ministres for administration; and Assembly oversight of force through enabling statutes. Enactment of these details has not been established.
Not to be added: a prime minister, second chamber, hereditary seats, weighted votes, lifetime appointments, a particular judiciary, or precise term limits.
The proposed Loi sur la protection universelle de la personne consciente would put universal enforcement against servitude into this framework. Its passage and any crusade remain unestablished.

journeys.title: Survival and Continuity
journeys.intro: From a dying Earth to a democracy that refuses to let anyone fall.

steps_v2.note: The catastrophe before the campaign.
Saved synthesization milestone; canon's turn to synthetic embodiment.
First colony beyond Sol.
The Great Sleeper's people become citizens (integration first observed).
First contact with the Fallen Empire that would humiliate the République.
Saturn's Assembly completed (corrected date).
Cosmogenesis still at level III in the latest save.

journeys.title: Unearthed Worlds
journeys.intro: The République's own excavations, in the order their chapters closed.

steps_v2.note: Grunur Ruins completed before the archive begins.
The peace token delivered.
The Oracle is answered.
The Huntress's blade recovered.
Mother Brain left to grow.
The Rubricator found.
The last Baol system found.
The Chronicles taken up.
S.I.D.N.I. purged.

journeys.title: Beyond the Rifts
journeys.intro: All ten République expeditions into astral rifts, in the order they finished, with the choices the saves remember.

steps_v2.note: First astral rift.
Genesis finished; new people settled.
The rift nearest Sol finished.
Chemical Wasteland finished.
Tropical Habitat finished.
Armand Noël stays behind with RIV.
The Fluid ends in loss.
The Baol homeworld cloaked.
The end of a universe observed.
The expedition finishes after the obelisk's destruction.

journeys.title: The Republic Grows
journeys.intro: Territory, subjects and partners, read from snapshot ownership.

steps_v2.note: Sol held in the earliest retained save.
First colony.
First unique system claimed.
Peaceful integration of 62 systems (first observed).
First war won; first vassal by war.
Victory over the Panuri; a protectorate.
Tortoka becomes a subject.
President of a ten-member federation of its own subjects.
Bilnoc's 32 systems join the République.
The first of three wars of subjugation is won.
307 systems, first in the galaxy.

journeys.title: Who Counts as a Person?
journeys.intro: Minds made, grown, simulated, enslaved or hidden — what the saves show the République actually did, beside what its canon says it believes.

steps_v2.note: Canon: conscious beings matter regardless of origin; a maker does not own what it makes.
Joining the Lumièran species does not erase a newcomer's face, culture or self (user clarification, 2026-11-09).
A dog-derived AI is a person, and Gestral continuity differs from Lumièran.
A stronger neighbour's people join as citizens; how consent was expressed is not specified.
Choices in a simulation, then real living beings: 100 Andari created.
An AI that ruled and killed a people asks to talk; the République opens communications.
A growing, unknown mind is monitored without harm.
A plantoid hive is hidden from extermination.
A subject at the centre of the servitude investigation.
A machine judge that killed its prisoners is purged: not every mind is spared.
The proposed universal protection of conscious persons — not enacted.
Whether a person may refuse continuation remains unresolved.

journeys.title: The Refusal of Loss
journeys.intro: From the Gommage to Cosmogenesis: the losses the record keeps, and the ones the République would not accept. Private motives are left unwritten.

steps_v2.note: A catastrophe taking ever younger people.
A brother who could not be preserved, and one who wants an end.
Canon's mission: that no one will die in the galaxy again — whether they consent or not.
Synthetic embodiment becomes the survival path.
A scientist lost to a rift returns, changed (first observed).
A century of digs reaches the last of an extinct people.
A rift gamble fails; scientist Alain Fontaine dies.
In another universe, a people is hidden rather than lost.
Overcoming even cosmic limits, with its moral limits undecided.

journeys.title: The Gardens of the Baol
journeys.intro: From a vanished living precursor to nine seeded Gaia worlds, alongside Éden's different origin.

steps_v2.note: Éden becomes a Gaia world — through abandoned alien terraforming, not the Baol.
The last Baol system is found; the relic follows.
First Nu-Baol life-seeding.
Azure Chalice seeded.
Terre seeded.
Pérennité seeded.
Fontaine seeded.
Nuitz's Treasure seeded.
The Wait seeded.
Églantine, a nuked world, seeded.
Where Nuitz Spoke seeded.
The newcomers join, and remain themselves.

journeys.title: The Question of Emancipation
journeys.intro: Following the République's anti-servitude principle through the saves: what is recorded, and what remains unproven. No law, casus belli or consent mechanism is recorded; each step says exactly what the archive shows.

steps_v2.note: The principle: conscious persons cannot be property. Proposed, not enacted.
A slavery-permitting theocracy becomes a protectorate after the Panuri war.
Tortoka, central to the servitude concern, becomes a subject.
Fifteen Lumièrans listed on the galactic slave market.
Bilnoc is integrated, the first of three.
Tortoka is integrated.
First war of subjugation declared; the saved goal is Blessed Torrent.
Five partners leave the federation; why is not recorded.
The Panuri Divine Theocracy, which allowed slavery and AI servitude until its last listed save, is integrated.
Breanne, a slavery-permitting state, and Zracon become protectorates.
Korinth, with the largest foreign Lumièran population, becomes a protectorate.
Servitude policies persist in four subjects. The question is open.

canon:esquie.title: Canon: Esquie
canon:esquie.text: The tamed L-Drake is **Esquie**, referred to as **he/him**. His nanite nature does not make those pronouns inappropriate. The user likes Maëlle riding him, echoing their relationship in Expedition 33. His presence brings affection and wonder into a civilization otherwise preoccupied with survival. [C4]

federation:name.note: Both name parts are kept: “Union of” has no placeholder, so a renderer that only fills placeholders would drop “Associated Nations”. The federation's start_date field is not used as a founding or joining date.

canon:federation-name.title: Canon: the federation's name
canon:federation-name.text: The République accepted an invitation to the **Union of Associated Nations**. Cooperation fits its desire to share survival, reduce unnecessary wars, and create a larger sphere in which people can live. The federation is not merely camouflage for a secret commitment to conquest. [C5]

canon:person:maelle:0.title: Canon: Maëlle Dessendre
canon:person:maelle:0.text: Her informal power nevertheless exceeds that of an ordinary officeholder. The intended feel is **“a goddess pretending to be a peer.”** This describes the asymmetry between her historic importance and her formal position among fellow citizens, not literal divinity. People may be legally equal and still find it extraordinarily hard to oppose the person who saved their lives.

canon:person:maelle:1.title: Canon: Maëlle Dessendre
canon:person:maelle:1.text: “Making death optional” can describe one attractive consequence of the technology, but it is incomplete as a statement of Maëlle's personality. The original characterization explicitly included bringing immortality to people **whether they consent or not**, supported by a democratic Lumièran electorate. Do not silently replace this with a fully voluntary liberal program.

canon:person:maelle:2.title: Canon: Maëlle Dessendre
canon:person:maelle:2.text: Maëlle's foundational ambition is that **“no one will die in the galaxy again.”** This is a universal extension of the rescue that saved the Lumièrans. Continued conscious existence, relationship, memory, and the possibility of another tomorrow are central goods. The mission is sincere, not a pretext for acquiring territory or enslaving people. [C1]

canon:person:gustave:0.title: Canon: Gustave
canon:person:gustave:0.text: Against a Fallen Empire that the République cannot defeat, his counsel is unequivocal: **“We can't face them.”** Endure humiliation, preserve Maëlle and the population, and keep working toward a solution. This is strategic patience with a purpose, not permanent submission.

canon:person:verso:0.title: Canon: Verso and pVerso
canon:person:verso:0.text: The original Verso dies in a war during the broader age of catastrophe. He cannot be stored. His loss therefore cannot be repaired by recovering a preserved original mind. Maëlle's attachment to him and the possibility that she feels responsible are central to the developing backstory; the exact circumstances of his death and the precise basis of her guilt remain unspecified. Do not invent a battle, order, betrayal, or particular act by Maëlle.

canon:person:verso:1.title: Canon: Verso and pVerso
canon:person:verso:1.text: An artificial Verso, sometimes called **pVerso** to distinguish him from the original, is created afterward. He spends a long period in a virtual environment, develops a relationship with Maëlle, and later receives a physical synthetic body. His existence is not the same historical event as restoring someone whose own mind was successfully preserved. [C2]

canon:person:monoco:0.title: Canon: Monoco and the Gestrals
canon:person:monoco:0.text: The original Verso created the first Gestrals. They are part of the Dessendres' history of robotics and companionship. Monoco is an AI whose personality is based on the family dog. Their warmth, loyalty, and sometimes dog-like affection matter to the campaign's emotional life. [C2]

canon:person:sciel-lune:0.title: Canon: Sciel and Lune
canon:person:sciel-lune:0.text: Sciel and Lune belong to the requested companion ensemble and appear in the visual conception alongside Gustave, Verso, and Monoco. Their formal offices and specific AU biographies have not been established. Their absence from an earlier name list does not erase them from the intended ensemble. Do not fabricate ministries, marriages, deaths, or military commands to fill the gap. [C3, C4]

canon:person:esquie:0.title: Canon: Esquie
canon:person:esquie:0.text: The tamed L-Drake is **Esquie**, referred to as **he/him**. His nanite nature does not make those pronouns inappropriate. The user likes Maëlle riding him, echoing their relationship in Expedition 33. His presence brings affection and wonder into a civilization otherwise preoccupied with survival. [C4]

canon:institution:republique:0.title: Canon: The Democratic République
canon:institution:republique:0.text: The democracy can sincerely endorse a coercive universal mission. The Lumièrans' support for Maëlle does not prove that everyone beyond their borders, or every dissenter within them, consents to what she intends. Preserve both popular legitimacy and the limits of what that legitimacy settles.

conversation:U1.title: User clarification, 2026-11-09
conversation:U1.text: Another note is that the Gaia transformations are caused by the Nu-Baol seeding, which I believe we got from an Astral rift event. We periodically acquire pops (including through Nu-Baol seeding) but they're quickly assimilated into the main Lumieran species. However, canonically, individuals still retain their physical appearance, culture, etc. (though they are also free to change their appearance).
conversation:U1.note: Undated canon adopted from this message: Newcomers who mechanically join the main Lumièran species keep their physical appearance, culture and individual identity, and remain free to change their appearance. How the saves bear on its other statements is a separate research excerpt, dated to the archive cutoff.

assessment:U1.title: Research assessment of the 2026-11-09 clarification (archive through 2390.07.01)

values: Player confirmation that the Gaia transformations were caused by Nu-Baol seeding — corroborated by the saves for four worlds; not for Éden (2242), which predates the Last Baol relic.
Player account that acquired pops are quickly assimilated into the main Lumièran species — consistent with the species reports, which list each newcomer species in one save only.

“which I believe we got from an Astral rift event” — explicitly tentative, and contradicted by the installed scripts and saves: life-seeding comes from activating the Last Baol relic, a Baol dig-trail reward. The Siege on Paradise rift yielded the Astral Cloaking edict.

assessment:U1.note: These are the atlas's findings from the saves and installed scripts, not the user's words.

open_threads.title: Study the Dendritian Chronicles
open_threads.text: The special project issued by the Chronicles of Dendrus is still listed among the République's open events in the 2454.05.05 save, as in every save since 2370.01.01. The chain has not progressed further.

open_threads.title: The Crystal Sphere
open_threads.text: The Azilash storyline is still in progress in the 2454.05.05 save: a crystal sphere was sent on 2352.01.01, the République holds a rift sphere, and the portal has not opened. No crystal rift near Sol and no completed arc is implied.

open_threads.title: Universal protection of conscious persons
open_threads.text: The war-powers instrument against servitude was embraced in concept. No save records its enactment. Between 2429 and 2452 the République fought three wars of subjugation, and it integrated a slavery-permitting subject, but the saves record no reasons for either. In the 2454.05.05 save four of its subjects still have servitude policies.

open_threads.title: The proposed constitution
open_threads.text: The Assemblée de la Continuité, the Conseil des Ministres and Assembly oversight of force remain proposals; only the democracy and the elected presidency are established.

open_threads.title: Verso's choice
open_threads.text: pVerso wants an eventual death. His final choice and Maëlle's response remain unwritten.

open_threads.title: The limits of Cosmogenesis
open_threads.text: The ambition is adopted, and the path is still at level III in the 2454.05.05 save. Which harms are acceptable, and the final outcome, are undecided.

open_threads.title: Terre's Nu-Baol newcomers
open_threads.text: The cause of Terre's Gaia change is now established: a Baol life-seeding completed on 2370.01.14, and Terre is the only world that became Gaia between the 2370.01.01 and 2370.07.01 saves. The flag does not name the planet, and the decision's 720-day enactment start is not saved. Unlike the other three seedings, no Nu-Baol species row is listed at Terre in the next save.

open_threads.title: When Esquie was named
open_threads.text: The hatchling's fleet is first called “Esquie” in the 2390.07.01 save; the naming happened after 2390.01.01, on an unrecorded date.

open_threads.title: How the Great Sleeper consented
open_threads.text: Peaceful integration is established canon and the saves show it (2270). How consent was expressed is not specified; no plebiscite is assumed.

open_threads.title: Lumièrans in servitude
open_threads.text: The discussed reconstruction of how Lumièrans came to be enslaved abroad is not proof of any individual's history. The archive now adds one slave-market listing of Lumièrans (2379.07.01) and Lumièran population counts in foreign states. Specific accusations still need specific evidence.

open_threads.title: Servitude inside the République's protectorates
open_threads.text: In the 2454.05.05 save Korinth, Pelx-Cradonian and Zracon hold AI in servitude, and Breanne and Pelx-Cradonian allow slavery; all four are République subjects. Korinth alone counts about 579 Lumièran pops. Whether any individual Lumièran there is held in servitude is not shown by the reports.

open_threads.title: Why the Union split
open_threads.text: Five members left the federation between the 2429.07.01 and 2430.01.01 saves, and a rival federation under Breanne was founded on 2430.12.25. The saves do not record why or in what order.

open_threads.title: Blessed Torrent's integration
open_threads.text: Blessed Torrent's protectorate has permitted integration since the 2443.07.01 save. It is still a separate subject in the 2454.05.05 save.

open_threads.title: The Sek-Lokkar wars
open_threads.text: Two wars against the Wandering Sek-Lokkar are active in the 2454.05.05 save. One has been running since 2429.07.01, the other since 2438.09.24. The République is not a belligerent in either.

open_threads.title: How the Khan's Throne was won
open_threads.text: The galaxy timeline records a Great Khan on 2421.03.18, and the République first holds the Khan's Throne relic in the 2423.07.01 save. No République war against the Khan is listed in the reports, and how the throne was obtained is not recorded.

archival_discoveries.title: Thread closed: Fix the Alien Vessel
archival_discoveries.text: “Fix the Alien Vessel” was listed from the 2390.07.01 to the 2395.01.01 save and is no longer listed.

archival_discoveries.title: Thread closed: Treasure Trove
archival_discoveries.text: The “Treasure Trove” project was listed again from the 2430.07.01 to the 2441.07.01 save and is no longer listed; its location and origin remain unresolved.

archival_discoveries.title: Thread closed: Volcanic Plane expedition
archival_discoveries.text: The Volcanic Plane expedition finished between the 2390.07.01 and 2391.01.01 saves.

archival_discoveries.title: “No active war” is now a dated observation
archival_discoveries.text: The v3 statement that no save records a République war was true at 2390.07.01. Three wars followed; the canon about their purpose is unchanged and unproven.

archival_discoveries.title: Life-seedings: four become nine
archival_discoveries.text: v3 counted four seedings, all through 2380. The flag records five more, the last on 2451.07.29.

archival_discoveries.title: Federation membership rewritten
archival_discoveries.text: v3's ten-member roster (2390.07.01) is kept as a dated observation. By 2454 the roster has changed: five members left in 2429–2430, two were integrated, and five subjects joined.

archival_discoveries.title: Tortoka integrated
archival_discoveries.text: v3 described a protectorate that did not permit integration. Integration was permitted from the 2418.07.01 save, and the country left the reports between the 2420.01.01 and 2420.07.01 saves.

archival_discoveries.title: Suter no longer unclaimed
archival_discoveries.text: v3's “unclaimed” described the 2390.07.01 save. Suter III became a République colony on 2414.06.01.

archival_discoveries.title: Kibbin no longer unexcavated
archival_discoveries.text: v3 said the Moon Base had no completed chapters and the system was unclaimed (true at 2390.07.01). The République has since excavated both Kibbin sites.

archival_discoveries.title: Rift reward clarified
archival_discoveries.text: The Siege on Paradise rift yielded the Astral Cloaking edict, not life-seeding; life-seeding comes from the Last Baol relic.

archival_discoveries.title: Terre's Gaia cause established
archival_discoveries.text: v2 said the cause was not retained. Life-seeding completed 2370.01.14, inside Terre's Continental → Gaia interval.

archival_discoveries.title: Life-seeding targets identified
archival_discoveries.text: v2 said the saves do not tie the relic's life-seeding to any world. The flag's four values match the Gaia changes of Mélèze, Azure Chalice, Terre and Pérennité.

archival_discoveries.title: Éden's Gaia change explained (not Nu-Baol)
archival_discoveries.text: Éden became Gaia between 2242.01.01 and 2242.07.01 through the Abandoned Terraforming colony chain (modifier abandoned_terraforming → gaia_world; “Resume Process” project listed 2226.07.01–2242.01.01). That is ninety years before the Last Baol relic.

highlights.title: The République in 2454
highlights.text: 307 systems, 73 colonies, 4072.92 pops, first in the galaxy. Maëlle is president in all 485 saves, and the République is at peace itself.

highlights.title: Three wars of subjugation, 2429–2452
highlights.text: The saved goals were Blessed Torrent, Breanne and Korinth. Each war ended with agreements dated the day it was won; the République's reasons are not recorded.

highlights.title: Bilnoc, Tortoka and the Panuri Theocracy integrated
highlights.text: Each disappeared after its agreement permitted integration, and its systems passed to the République (2416, 2420, 2431).

highlights.title: The Union divided
highlights.text: Five federation members left between two 2429 saves, and a rival federation led by Breanne formed. The République's 2442 war was fought against most of it. By 2454 the Union is the République and nine of its subjects.

highlights.title: Lumièrans abroad, and on the slave market
highlights.text: A newly found slave-market listing of 15 Lumièrans (2379), growing Lumièran populations in Korinth and Glebsig, and servitude policies that persist in subjects.

highlights.title: Five more Gaia worlds
highlights.text: Fontaine, Nuitz's Treasure, The Wait, Églantine and Where Nuitz Spoke were seeded by the Last Baol relic. Twelve République Gaia worlds are now accounted for.

highlights.title: Kibbin's shielded world opened
highlights.text: The Moon Base and Abandoned Ecumenopolis digs (2428–2437) produced the Miniature Galaxy relic and a new colony.

highlights.title: The Tomb of Zarqlan
highlights.text: Six chambers excavated at Nekkar; the Head of Zarqlan relic followed.

highlights.title: Eleven more rift expeditions
highlights.text: Volcanic Plane finished, followed by ten newly explored rifts, from the Lone Object to The Garden. Each has its chapters and retained choices.

highlights.title: Relays and gateways
highlights.text: The latest save lists 229 République hyper relays and 18 gateways. Their milestones are grouped, not listed one by one.

infrastructure.note: Hyper relay and gateway milestones are grouped under “Le Réseau”; each remains in the Chronicle as a routine record.
